A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DORNet, with readable and matchable main text, equations, tables and figures. However, both end with references and contain no referenced appendices. This limits comparison of v4's announced cross-task and additional noise experiments.

before.justification: v1 reports original DORNet and DORNet-T benchmark results, qualitative comparisons, efficiency measurements and ablations.

after.justification: v4 retains original benchmark results and ablations and additionally reports a noise-level sensitivity experiment in Figure 7.

M1.justification: The documented router, degradation-kernel generation, DOFT fusion, training losses and DORNet-T channel reduction remain unchanged. Degradation Awareness is renamed Degradation-Oriented Fusion without a specified procedural change.

E1.justification: The demonstrated dataset coverage remains RGB-D-D, TOFDSR and NYU-v2. v4 Section 4.3 additionally states that the method is implemented for pan-sharpening and depth completion, but defers the experiments to an absent appendix. Their actual empirical coverage cannot be reliably assessed.

E2.justification: Quantitative comparator membership is retained. However, the matched RGB-D-D qualitative comparison drops DKN, FDKN, FDSR and SUFT; the TOFDSR qualitative comparison additionally drops DJFR and CUNet. Both revised visual comparisons retain DCTNet, SFG and SGNet alongside the proposed models.

E3.justification: The reported RGB-D-D test size changes from 449 to 405 pairs. v4 adds a five-level Gaussian-noise sweep from 0.04 to 0.16 with fixed blur. It also explicitly applies noise to upsampled LR depth, whereas v1 describes LR depth without that distinction. These statements do not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v4 Figure 7 adds sensitivity analysis across noise strengths, extending the earlier fixed-noise comparison. Figure 8 adds error maps for the existing RGB-D-D example. The component, loss, DOFT-recursion and kernel-generator ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty bars. Gaussian-noise standard deviations describe input corruption, not statistical uncertainty.

E6.justification: Noisy RGB-D-D RMSE changes from 4.57 to 4.08 cm for SFG, 4.25 to 4.24 for DORNet-T and 3.69 to 3.68 for DORNet, reversing SFG's ordering relative to DORNet-T. Noisy TOFDSR values change from 5.16 to 5.07 for DORNet-T and 4.48 to 4.47 for DORNet. Figure 7 adds noise-sweep results. Noise-free, NYU-v2 and ablation scores remain unchanged; the evaluation revisions prevent treating the changed values as verified same-setting gains.

T1.justification: Equations 1–11 retain the same mathematical definitions and operations, with notation changes such as the convolution symbol. Neither supplied version contains formal theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that self-supervised degradation learning and degradation-guided RGB-D fusion improve depth super-resolution under unknown degradation. The Blind title, explicit label-free wording and reorganized contribution bullets clarify the existing claims without substantively changing their scope.

C2.justification: v4 explicitly motivates implicit degradation learning through the unavailability of degradation labels. It also characterizes NYU-v2 performance as comparable, replacing v1's description as superior to most approaches. The central degradation-map interpretation remains unchanged, and neither version adds a substantive limitations discussion.

D1.justification: v4 Section 4.2 newly explains that available baseline scores are quoted from papers and other methods are retrained using released code. Section 3.3 additionally identifies residual blocks and channel attention within the residual group. The optimizer, learning rate, loss weights and RTX 4090 hardware remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The bibliography adds six works, including DCDepth and Completion as Enhancement, and removes three, including Mutual-Structure for Joint Filtering. Related-work examples are shortened, while the positioning around degradation representations for RGB-D fusion remains substantially the same.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion are substantially rewritten, and terminology is revised throughout the method description. The experimental narrative merges the real-world comparisons, separates noise robustness and inserts a generalization section. The title, author list and contribution organization also change.

P2.justification: v4 redraws the framework diagrams, changes error-map coloring, and reorganizes Tables 1–2 by noise condition instead of dataset. It compresses the real-world qualitative montages, adds RGB-D-D error maps and introduces the noise-sensitivity plot. Together these substantially revise the visual presentation, although much underlying content is retained.

improvement.justification: The new noise-sensitivity evidence, clearer method explanations and diagrams, and disclosure of baseline-result provenance provide a limited improvement in support and readability. The central method and results remain largely stable. Reduced qualitative comparator coverage, unexplained evaluation revisions and missing appendices limit the gains; the announced cross-task generalization cannot be credited from the supplied evidence.
